salient_findings: Originating from the left ventricular lateral wall
key_facts: Denied fever, weight loss, dyspnea, or other symptoms
Chest radiograph revealed no active lung lesions
Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a left ventricular mass
Contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography showed focal contrast enhancement

shortlist.label: Cardiac Myxoma
shortlist.why_kept: most common primary cardiac tumor, mobile and pedunculated mass on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Left Ventricular Thrombus
shortlist.why_kept: possible cause of left ventricular mass, especially with focal contrast enhancement on CT

shortlist.label: Papillary Fibroelastoma
shortlist.why_kept: benign cardiac tumor, can appear as a mobile mass on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: rare benign cardiac tumor, can cause left ventricular mass

shortlist.label: Metastatic Tumor
shortlist.why_kept: possible cause of left ventricular mass, although less common than primary cardiac tumors

raw.rationale: The presence of a mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass originating from the left ventricular lateral wall with focal contrast enhancement on computed tomography is most consistent with a cardiac myxoma, which is a type of benign tumor.

rejected.label: Left Ventricular Thrombus
rejected.why: Thrombi are typically irregular and not pedunculated

rejected.label: Papillary Fibroelastoma
rejected.why: These tumors are usually smaller and more often found on the valves

rejected.label: Fibroma
rejected.why: Fibromas are typically solid, non-pedunculated masses

rejected.label: Metastatic Tumor
rejected.why: Metastatic tumors to the heart are more common in patients with known cancer and often involve multiple sites
